messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw KV-cache memory keep creeping up on long-context runs when we use paging + reuse. Reprobed on H100 and RTX6000, behavior diverges.
shyam: repro steps? was this on the kv-paged-attn branch or mainline? :thinking_face:
maria: mainline with the paged-kv opt enabled. short repro: run the long-dialog workload (200k tokens total across sessions), enable kv_page_size=64M, reuse_window=32, and watch device mem.
maria: on H100 mem plateaus after some evictions like expected. on RTX6000 it slowly grows ~10-20MB / 10k tokens until OOM.
kevin: can you paste logs where eviction happens? suspect we missed an index unpin path.
maria: paste below — trimmed:

```
[2026-06-04T10:13:42Z] kv: evict_page idx=4123 owner=conn-73 last_use=102334 free=1
[2026-06-04T10:13:42Z] kv: map_set idx=4123 -> page=0x7f4a31b0000
[2026-06-04T10:13:43Z] kv: evict_page idx=4123 owner=conn-73 last_use=102336 free=0
[2026-06-04T10:13:44Z] kv: page_table[idx=4123].refcount=0 -> 1 (realloc)
[2026-06-04T10:13:45Z] kv: hole_counter ++ -> 1
```

maria: that 'hole_counter' increment looks suspicious — on H100 we didn't see holes.
perf-bot: perf snapshot uploaded — https://perf.internal/reports/1867034821
perf-bot: top diff: kv::evict() slower on RTX6000 by 23% and memory churn +12MB per 10k tokens
tao: I ran a bisect yesterday: regressions start around driver 525.x on RTX. H100 test used driver 545.x. Could be driver interaction with cudaMemAdvise or with migration.
kevin: 525.x known to return stale cudaPointerGetAttributes for managed allocations sometimes. If our page table stores a 32-bit packed field (gpu_id<<24 | local_idx) maybe wrap or stale mapping emerges.
shyam: oof. we do pack a tag with 8 bits gpu + 24 bits index in page_table_entry to save space. If local_idx increments past 16M pages on long workloads, it wraps. Reminds me of the wrap bug we fixed for slotmap a while back.
maria: repro on rtx: I forced allocation churn with this little python loop, you'll see free list length fluctuate but hole_counter keeps increasing:

```
for _ in range(50000):
    model.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=256)
```

maria: attaching a short dump of page table entries (idx -> tag):
```
4122 -> 0x0100a12b
4123 -> 0x0100a12c
4124 -> 0x00000000  # zeroed but referenced
4125 -> 0x0100a12d
```
kevin: 4124 zeroed but referenced — that's the hole. looks like an eviction raced with reuse path which reallocated backing memory but never set table entry under RTX.
tao: hypothesis: cuda driver reorder of writes + our non-atomic write to page_table + consumer on another stream reads stale zero. H100 memory model behaves differently or has implicit coherency.
shyam: possible fix: write with atomic store or write-release + memory fence on host side before enqueueing reuse. or set reserved 'invalid' tag value and avoid zero meaning free.
maria: small patch i tried locally (in kv_pager.cpp):

```
- page_table[idx] = 0; // free
+ // mark free with sentinel then fence to avoid transient zero reads from GPU
+ page_table[idx] = PAGE_TAG_FREE_SENTINEL;
+ std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_release);
```

maria: with that patch RTX run stopped growing mem in my quick test (10k tokens). need wider runs.
kevin: good. also add ASSERT that tag != 0 in consumer path and log a stack trace when seen. helps track where zero sneaks in.
shyam: we should also consider upgrading the allocator metadata to 64-bit tag to avoid wrap entirely. but that's invasive and touches hot path.
tao: for short-term mitigation, change PAGE_TAG_FREE_SENTINEL != 0 and make zero reserved for 'invalid/uninitialized' so we catch it in CI.
maria: agreed. I'll open a draft PR with three things: sentinel write + release fence, ASSERT where consumer sees zero, and doc comment about 24-bit packing risk.
kevin: please also add a targeted CI job that runs the long-dialog loop on an RTX6000 instance (if available) overnight.
perf-bot: CI job scheduled: kv-long-dialog-rtx-nightly
maria: thanks — PR incoming. I'll post links and paste more logs after the larger repro. if someone from infra can spin an rtx instance for the full 200k token run that would be great.
kevin: pinging @tao for infra. tao — can you allocate one?
tao: yes, will allocate rtx-6000-1 for tonight and enable driver 525.x to match repro. will attach nvprof and cuda-memcheck logs.
shyam: great, also add a small microbenchmark that repeatedly sets and reads page_table entry under multi-stream stress so we can detect ordering differences in CI.
maria: perfect. moving to PR now. thanks all :rocket:
